name: A Certified Three-Piece Separating-Edge Obstruction
statement: For the fixed $289$-concept rooted factor $C$, repair $c=290$ inside the face on $J=\{1,2,5,6,7,8\}$ and form the marked two-layer piece $K$. Then $|T|=41$, $|K|=330$, $K\setminus D$ is connected, and the exact edge profile is $(0,1,0,1,0)$. Every proper old-coordinate elementary image retaining $D$ peels to $D$. Gluing $K$, an endpoint-reversed copy of $K$, and the fixed $581$-concept piece of profile $(0,1,1,0,0)$ along their common edge produces an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness with $1237$ concepts and isometric dimension $37$. Deleting the edge leaves exactly three components, and every nonempty-coordinate reduction is dismantlable ample.
proof: The repaired-face theorem supplies ampleness, positivity, the three zero entries, $\ell_u=1$, and all private-minor retention tests. A stored complete corner order ending at $u$, independently certified by its nonclashing out-map, supplies $t_u=1$. Relative minimality forces $K\setminus D$ to be connected, since otherwise its proper convex pieces would each peel to $D$ and their orders would concatenate. The three profiles are pairwise compatible but all fail retention, so the exact three-piece separator construction gives a nonpeelable union whose every proper pc-minor peels. Counting the shared edge gives $330+330+581-4=1237$ and the disjoint private blocks give dimension $37$. Private-coordinate reductions are positive by closure; the common-edge reduction is a one-point amalgam of two rooted-positive copies of the repaired face and the positive core, so it is positive as well.
